scope: Frozen r1090 Classic/Feyz. Native original bundled MP3 clocks, explicitly labelled generated PCM, genuine canonical IDB and cross-tab durability, full deployment ZIP construction, real installed service worker and cold offline reload with server sockets disabled. Superseded runs are not release evidence.
limitations: Disposable Linux Chromium, Classic/Feyz at390×844 and320×640, exact served production shell/modules. Physical Samsung/Android, perceptual audio quality and remote paid membership are not measured.

Device PINs are labelled test inputs. Enrollment/verification/commit/reset run through the actual production adapter and PIN helpers; a labelled provider stub is used solely to prove that provider mode hides and rejects device management.

One synthetic WAV is an IndexedDB preservation sentinel, never presented as a recitation. Native clocks, transports and gate animation timers remain unchanged; reduced motion is enabled only for explicitly marked fixture groups.
Disposable Linux Chromium, Classic/Feyz at 390×844 CSS pixels. No physical Samsung, Android screen-lock, real-device autoplay or audible recitation quality claim.

Generated two-second PCM tones occupy disposable personal-recording keys. Native HTMLMediaElement clocks, currentTime, play, pause and ended are not replaced; application progress is observed after native completion.

Race cases call actual production timeline onclick/exported restart and terminal APIs within one page.evaluate task. Separate canonical cases call SukunSessionState.command and assert accepted:true. These measure command boundaries, not physical fast tap timing.

Preparation cases hold an actual reads-only readwrite transaction in disposable sukunRec/clips and observe real pending readonly requests after source admission; exact r422 pre-admission receipt timing is covered separately by controlled source tests. Mixed cases run shipped rain and both WebAudio frequencies with unchanged context clocks.
Production source files are served byte-for-byte with service workers blocked. Audio observation wrappers only log native calls/events and return the original results.

Exact Classic/Feyz application scripts, normal visual CSS, and genuine Chromium native media clocks at 384×691. Generated six-second tones occupy three isolated personal recording slots; no user recordings, images, browser profile or health report is read.

Race matrix calls actual production exported navigation and SukunSessionState command APIs within one browser task. This establishes command ownership, not physical fast tap timing. A genuine native personal recording is observed through unchanged media clocks.

The engineering fixture controls device TTS, which is forbidden for these personal recording scenarios. Service workers are blocked; physical Android screen locking, speaker audibility, OS audio focus and SW activation are not measured.
The separate Node command-scope suite verifies independently paused background providers. This browser run focuses on the sole single-name captured mix that previously stranded the wheel controls.
Disposable Linux headless Chromium with an actual installed service worker; Classic/Feyz. No physical Android, lock-screen or audible-quality claim.

Network becomes explicitly offline only after worker installation; the isolated HTTP fixture also closes new sockets so service-worker fetches cannot bypass browser context offline emulation. No online bundled find/play is called; the worker mandatory runtime cache alone must contain all six original MP3 files.
Each original MP3 is verified by SHA-256 and a small native currentTime advance, then explicitly stopped. No full recitation completion or successful repeat credit is claimed.
Saved templates and favorites use the unmodified canonical store while offline, including a fresh page. User recordings, microphone and unrelated personal data are not used.

One labelled storage failure is injected only into the canonical template database transaction method; two actual pointer clicks verify the error message and successful retry. The original method is restored before retry.

This suite verifies the current installed release and an old launcher URL. Historical release switching and installation under real mobile bandwidth/quota are covered only by controlled tests or remain device work.

Disposable Chromium at390×844 Classic/Feyz, two pages sharing one actual origin/storage. Production files are served byte-for-byte; service workers blocked. No personal user data, physical Samsung behavior, audible playback or screen-lock behavior is measured.

Normal writes use the actual unchanged asynchronous store APIs or public Save/favorite buttons. Fixture seed writes/reset the real canonical IDB record explicitly; direct mirror changes are never treated as normal backend writes. No localStorage, production timer, Date, WebLock or IDB API is patched.

One explicitly labelled async-Save test holds an actual separate native IDB guard transaction to expose a pending-write interval. It releases that transaction before awaiting the production save; audio is never started.

Disposable native Chromium390×844 Classic/Feyz, byte-identical production files and genuine IndexedDB transactions, JSON serialization, maintenance leases, SHA-256 asset verification and ZIP Blob construction. Service workers blocked; no user data or physical Android is used.

Only compatibility-mirror writes throw a labelled controlled QuotaExceededError. An IDB transaction observer delegates unchanged; one native write transaction is held to expose a pending read interval. One same-origin asset response is held to expose ZIP privacy timing. Production timers and Date are not replaced. The shared device-speech fixture is installed but no speech/audio completion is driven by this suite. A final labelled malformed canonical record verifies fail-closed behavior; normal saves use the unchanged store API.

Full-site export executes the actual production exporter over every inventory file and actual canonical personal JSON. The first ZIP member is decoded to verify its saved templates/favorites; per-file deployment hashes are enforced by the production exporter. Audio playback and physical lock-screen behavior are not measured.
